domain.headline: VP Vance said Sep 3 Iran's Hormuz control is 'effectively gone' and ruled out talks unless Tehran halts shipping attacks, but Kpler data show just ~5 Hormuz transits on Sep 1 versus a 10-day average of ~14, undercutting the claim. QatarEnergy force majeure now extends into early November; route-normalised freight and war-risk costs remain unavailable.

sources.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October
sources.note: No newer source-verified QatarEnergy force-majeure notice was approved in the Aug 18 review; carry the Reuters July 23 notice through mid-September and keep the later mid-October extension as unconfirmed preparation.

sources.title: Edison: QatarEnergy extends force majeure
sources.note: LNG Industry reported on Sep 1 that Edison received a further QatarEnergy force-majeure notice covering five additional cargoes; the reported total is 29 cargoes and the period extends into early November. This manual-reviewed event is carried because no automated QatarEnergy endpoint is approved.

sources.title: Strait of Hormuz commodity vessel transits stay in single digits, data shows
sources.note: Business Recorder reported Kpler data showing only 5 vessels transited Hormuz on Sep 1 (4 entered, 1 exited, no liquid tankers), versus a 10-day average of about 14; this replaces the stale Aug 27 Foreign Policy Journal weekly count.

sources.title: 'I Wouldn't Call it a War': Vance Downplays Conflict With Iran, Even as Strikes Continue
sources.note: Time reported VP Vance told a Sep 3 White House press briefing that Iran's Hormuz control is 'effectively gone,' a 'diminishing asset,' ruling out talks unless Tehran halts shipping attacks; he voiced 'extreme skepticism' of Iran's account of the Sep 1 Sirik wedding strike.
